title: WEBMASTER@ a manifesto for everyone
excerpt: I'm reclaiming the title of 'webmaster' as the multidisciplinary creator who designs, develops, writes, and advocates for their own corner of the web and will save the world. Tracing the history from 1993 to the present, I argue that anyone can become a webmaster with minimal tools. Webmastery is an act of digital repatriation and human agency against corporate platforms and AI orchestration.
content_html:
A week ago, when I was working on my project for HTML Day 2026 I stumbled upon this passage from an essay on blink and marquee tags:

At the time, there was a new breed of web professionals proudly labeled “webmasters.” Part designer, part developer and part evangelist, webmasters held enough esoteric knowledge about the web to manage, edit and create websites, both large and small.
— Jay Hoffman (August 28th, 2017)

And that's when everything clicked for me.

Over the past year, I've written dozens of articles on the Independent Web. Forty-two essays on principles, technical tutorials, accessibility, and advocacy.

And, in a way, it has all been leading to this manifesto. Only through months of research and getting to know many kind and talented people and building things myself have I finally understood the true power of the webmaster.

I think this will be the most important thing I'll ever write, and I wish to share it with you. With everyone.

Part One: THE PAST

The earliest webmasters were unauthorized, self-taught, one-person operations. The first webmaster was a woman, Stanford librarian Louise Addis.

i. ORIGINS (1993)

It was a few years after Tim Berners-Lee christened the first web server at CERN at the end of 1990, and published the first website info.cern.ch on August 6th, 1991[1].

The webmaster was first understood as the Internet's equivalent to the real-world postmaster.

"Other protocols have defacto standards for well known mailbox names, such as USENET@domain for NNTP (see [RFC977]), and WEBMASTER@domain for HTTP (see [HTTP])."
— RFC 2142, "Mailbox Names for Common Services, Roles and Functions," Dave Crocker, Internet Mail Consortium. (May 1997)

This RFC—alongside <POSTMASTER@domain> (required by RFC 822)—is what cemented "webmaster" as the canonical, protocol-level point-of-contact role for a website.

"The word “webmaster” comes from a similar role defined in the original specification for email called the postmaster, which in turn comes from the similarly named government position Postmaster General. You can think of the postmaster as an email administrator. The idea being that you can email postmater[sic] @ some domain, and always be connected directly to somebody that could fix a problem with the email. That remains a reserved name today on any email inbox. The webmaster served a pretty similar purpose on the web."
— Jay Hoffman, "What Happened to the Webmaster" (June 16, 2020)

And thus, webmaster@domain was already the de facto email inbox address tied to the HTTP protocol itself.

The label and title quickly grew into something far more than that, though.

"At first it referred to that frustrated techie who set up the rogue Web server without company authorization, coded HTML by hand in a text editor, FTP'd the files to the server, and in his spare time answered all the incoming corporate e-mails, usually also without company authorization."
— Brian Wold, "What Happened to the Webmaster? (And other misleading titles)" (May 12, 2006)

ii. GOLDEN AGE (1994-2001)

The era that conjures "webmaster" most strongly began in the mid 90's, as Beverly Hills Internet was launched, now known as GeoCities.

"[T]he point about the web before social networks or before Web 2.0 is not that you had a profile on GeoCities, but that you had a chance to build your cyber home outside of it, you could exist and grow outside of a centralized service."
— Olia Lialina, quoted in Cybercultural by Richard MacManus (March 7, 2025)

A culture developed as people realized anybody could make their own website. 88x31 buttons, blinkies, .GIFs, web rings, visitor counters, guestbooks. All originate from this time.

"In 1996, the web was littered with black-and-yellow-striped animated .gifs reveling in metaphors of road construction... 'This site under construction' was the default home page disclaimer, until everyone realized that the inherent nature of the web was that it would be perpetually under construction."
— Fresher Styles for Web Designers, O'Reilly (December 2008)

While GeoCities is fondly remembered now, it certainly had its problems and issues. Similarly, there were other platforms at the time as well, such as Tripod, Angelfire, and Homestead. It can be easy to revise history into an idealized monoculture.

"It was not a paradise for early web makers. It was not even a good web hosting service. It was free and not worse than others, that's why webmasters endured the pain of clumsy page builders, interventions from commercial scripts being injected into their pages, accidental file deletions, etc…"
— "GeoCities' Afterlife and Web History," by Olia Lialin, One Terabyte of Kilobyte Age (July 30, 2019)

Over 38 million pages were deleted when Yahoo shut down the platform in 2009.

iii. THE DECLINE (2008-2020)

As sites grew and the Internet evolved from the expectation of a handful of HTML files located in /var/www/html/ into instead a complex beast of software and content management systems, the "one person does everything" model stopped being the default, and the title became a culture-war topic among web professionals.

Schisms grew from the complexity. The Internet became a vector for business, and then the way to make money as the dotcom bubble inflated. People needed to specialize, whether that was to design for the front-end, or program and administrate the server from the back-end. You needed usability specialists and network engineers and search engine optimizers.

Dammit Jim, I’m a Webmaster, not a Digital Government Web Content Communications and Application Development Knowledge Management Specialist! ...or am I?
Is the term webmaster an accurate description of the responsibilities of today’s web professional, or is that moniker just a quaint artifact from the simpler, earliest days of the web where someone akin to a similarly quaint notion of a Ringmaster juggled a circus of unwieldy text, spinning logos and blinking text?
— David Kitzmiller, FCC Webmaster, Mastering the Web: An Old-Fashioned Notion? (August 12, 2010)

Perhaps the clearest and most citable marker of the term's formal retirement from mainstream professional use is when Google rebranded "Google Webmasters" to "Google Search Central" in 2020. An institutional funeral.

"Merriam-Webster claims the first known use of the word 'webmaster' was in 1993, years before Google even existed. However, the term is becoming archaic, and according to the data found in books, its use is in sharp decline. A user experience study we ran revealed that very few web professionals identify themselves as webmasters anymore. They're more likely to call themselves Search Engine Optimizer (SEO), online marketer, blogger, web developer, or site owner, but very few 'webmasters.' In brainstorming our new name, we realized that there's not one term that perfectly summarizes the work people do on websites."
— Google Search Central Blog (Nov 12, 2020)

Part Two: NOW

It is your innate human right to create.

All of the above was pretext for this: You can be a webmaster right now. You can create a website right now. Yes, you. Your website can look however you want it to, and function in any way you want. It can have whatever you want on it.

You can look up tutorials, and you can have your questions answered by humans just by joining forums, IRC channels, and independent platforms. The act of creating and learning inherently places you in the community.

prelude: The Deception

Generally speaking, we have been deceived into thinking many broad falsehoods:

Regarding the webmaster:

  1. The Internet has become too complex for a single person to master all aspects of it.
  2. You must use a certain tool or platform to properly be part of this movement.

Regarding the Internet:

  1. Technology is inherently addictive, and brings us harm.
  2. In order to stay connected to others online, we must use corporate social media platforms, become the product, and surrender our privacy.
  3. The Internet is primarily falsehoods, misinformation, and meaningless spam content.

Regarding us:

  1. Most of us are incapable of learning technical, scientific, mathematical concepts.
  2. Those of us who are knowledgeable are reluctant to share information, and hostile to beginners.

When plainly laid out like this, it's easy to see how we've been conned into a cynical, pessimistic—even misanthropic view of things. Companies worth billions of dollars have a bottom line that depends on the general population to continue believing all of the above.

Our perspective on technology and other people has been greatly distorted into the negative. In reality, the Internet has terabytes of high-quality resources to learn from. There are thousands of people just like you looking for connection, hungry for a better vision of the future, wanting to cultivate nourishing hobbies. You are so capable.

The idea that one person cannot master all aspects of the web, as the webmaster was once known to, is demonstrably false.

Be optimistic about your capabilities and the willingness of others to help you. Be skeptical of anybody who attempts to divide or gatekeep, proclaiming the mandated use or superiority of a specific tool or platform.

Likewise, I want to note that searching for "return of the webmaster" in 2026 may lead you to discussions of the "agentic web" or "orchestration," a euphemism for somebody who employs generative AI to do the multidisciplinary work that comes with being a webmaster. Those who manage a stack of expensive large language models, those who are prompt engineers for static site generators, and those who neglect to take the time to learn for themselves, unwilling to put in the effort themselves (or thinking they're incapable to).

That's not what this is. My manifesto is not about becoming an orchestrator. Being a webmaster means becoming a sovereign creator. We are not reclaiming the title of "webmaster" only to then offload the work and art onto chatbots. We are reclaiming it because it is the only title that remains which still carries the weight of total, unapologetic human agency over our digital lives.

a. The Bare Minimum is All You Need

To be a Webmaster, you need a computer, a text editor, and a way to host. That's it.

You don't need a degree in computer science. You don't need a $50/month subscription to a proprietary builder. You don't even need the money to buy a domain name if you don't have the cash.

  1. Use https://freedns.afraid.org/ to get a free domain.
  2. Throw your files up on Neocities or Nekoweb or web 1.0 hosting.
  3. Write your HTML in Notepad. Edit your CSS in TextEdit.

If you don't have a computer or Internet yourself, you could be sitting in a public library on a recycled Chromium machine and still you have everything you need to become a Webmaster. There are not gatekeepers at the doors of the World Wide Web. Like many other things in life, the only lock is the one we put on our own ambitions.

A Webmaster is not just a developer. You are a UX/UI designer, you are a writer and editor, you are an accessibility specialist, and an advocate for others to reclaim their digital autonomy. You are a creator, rather than a consumer. And you are capable of all these things.

You will wrestle with semantic markup to make a page accessible. You will agonize over typeface kerning and colour palettes. You will write prose and publish your weird obsessions and link to your Internet neighbours. You will manage server logs, tweak the .htaccess file, and you will decide and design the architecture of your digital home.

This is not a career path, this is a craft. This is the last best multidisciplinary sandbox, both creative and technical, all rendered on an index.html.

And there is no wrong answer. Serve your website over the Gemini protocol. SSH into the Tildeverse and build a terminal-based homepage alongside strangers. Set up a homelab in your closet using the old, defunct family computer. There are a million ways to do this. The only wrong answer is sitting on the sidelines believing you don't belong in the arena with us.

b. The Last Public Square

Corporate social media platforms we used to call the "new public square" have been astroturf'd, bulldozed, and sold to the highest-bidding fascist oligarch. Your existence is a rental, your voice is a throttled lottery. Your so-called "community" is at the mercy of a billionaire's whim.

Building your own website is an act of digital repatriation.

Creating your own corner of the Internet reclaims one of the only mediums where we retain freedom, creativity, and autonomy.

With the plethora of hosting options available, you can migrate if terms of service change to your disliking. There's no pay-to-play visibility. There's just you, text, and the open protocols of the web.

c. The Myth of Incompetence

The most effective way the power structures of our age have oppressed us is by making us feel as though we are stupid, as though we are incapable of learning.

Many of us have been convinced coding is arcane magic, that servers are eldritch horrors, and that computer science is reserved for child prodigies and those who are privileged to just "naturally get it."

A user who is afraid of the machine and doubts their own capabilities is one that will surrender and pay for a solution.

You are not incapable. There is a lot to learn, yes. And the technologies are deep. But do not forget we are still living in the golden age of human knowledge—endless free resources, tutorials, wikis, and forums are available at your fingertips.

I will repeat myself and say the only barrier that exists is the one you construct in your mind.

You require grit, determination, and a "why." This is your why. The desire to express yourself. The hunger to build something truly of your own. The need to connect with other humans.

d. Universalism

Let me be clear: this is not about "IndieWeb" specs, it isn't about the "Small Web" or "SmolWeb." It isn't a retro-revival nostalgia trip, pining for GeoCities and AOL dial-up tones.

Those are all labels, clubs, and memberships. Standards with elitism and in-group and cliques and gatekeeping as a result.

What I'm talking about is universal. It's not about specific mechanics, it's about a philosophy. It is a big tent.

It doesn't matter if you speak English. It doesn't matter if you don't know how to spell words right in your native tongue. It doesn't matter if you don't know a single line of JavaScript, either.

And it certainly doesn't matter if you think you have "nothing interesting to say." I promise you do. All humans have value, we have our hobbies, our frustrations, our obsessions and small thoughts. Putting this in writing on a page you build with your own hands means you're contributing to a richer, stranger, more wonderful ecosystem.

e. Those Who Came Before

I stand on the shoulders of giants. I am not the first to write a web manifesto, nor the last. I myself am nobody special, nor anybody with authority. I am mere conduit for a message that desperately needs to be heard.

I give credit to Tantek Çelik, Amber Case, Aaron Parecki, Crystal Beasley, and Kevin Marks for founding IndieWebCamp in Portland, Oregon in 2011.

I give credit to Daniel Murray's melonking.net as a foundational "web revival" artifact.

"[The web revival] is a riff on the 20th century American folk music revival, and it implies that early personal sites, like those hosted on GeoCities, were culturally significant as digital folk art."
— Daniel Murray (Melonking), quoted in New_ Public (September 7, 2025)

I give credit to webmistress Sadness, who has been sharing resources on web mastery for years, and was the founder of the now defunct Yesterweb, served as many people's first experience of the indie-web-crafting scene.

"In the earlier iterations of this manifesto, I made the mistake of focusing too heavily on the creation of personal websites as the main method of fighting against the exploitative capitalist hellscape that has become our Internet... For example, we can work on transforming social relations online."
— Sadness, Internet manifesto (May 2023)

I give credit to James G., who has been blogging about the independent Internet for over six years, who hosts the podcast Wonders of Webweaving, and who has recently founded the Web Writers' Collective, which is open to anyone.

I give credit to Alexandra and Kaylee for the community and resources of 32-bit Café. I give credit to Adam Newbold for the community and services of omg.lol.

There are hundreds of people who have dedicated thousands of hours in trying to make the web more human and joyous for all.

f. Saving the World

We can create a more human web right now. The world is in dire straits, and I'm reminded of the words of Carl Sagan, coincidentally written at the dawn of the webmaster:

“In our obscurity, in all this vastness, there is no hint that help will come from elsewhere to save us from ourselves.”
— Carl Sagan, Pale Blue Dot (1994)

There are those who see the act of webmastery as "only" a hobby and pastime—and I say this is not mutually exclusive to world-saving. The personal is political. Our ability to maintain our joy and ourselves is, itself, resistance.

Here is another falsehood I want to emphasize: Our right to freely express ourselves is never a guarantee. The past thirty years of the Internet have been an explosive, chaotic experiment in the commons and the human condition. But the freedom of expression we've been granted is not a given or perpetual promise, and it is extremely foolish to think we will have this for the next ten years, let alone forever.

Start as you are, with what you have, while you still have time to do so.

Exercise your innate human right to create.

Be a developer. Be a designer. Be a writer. Be a systems administrator. Be a philosopher. Be a Webmaster.

It is the most punk rock, anti-establishment, liberating thing you can do in the 21st century. And yeah, it is fucking awesome.

Now, go build something.

My Other IndieWeb Essays

Over the past year I've written forty-two essays on this subject. Here are the ones I think are most worth a beginner's time.

Starting Out

  • What I Have Learned Being on the IndieWeb for a Month: Small technical joys that turned solitude into dialogue, and treating the Internet like a personal playground and lab.
  • Resources for the Personal Web: A Follow-Up Guide: Blogging platforms, search engines that prioritize small sites, and directories for finding like-minded creators.
  • Softcore First, Hardcore Eventually: A Ladder for the IndieWeb: Why you should climb the rungs progressively instead of choosing between easy platforms and full technical independence on day one.
  • The 1% Rule: An Open Letter to Everyone Who Doesn't Post Anything Online: A call to action for the 99% of internet users who consume but never create.
  • You Don't Have to Blog: Your website can be shrines, art, or anything else. You don't need to write a single word to belong here.

Community and Connection

  • Won't You Be My Neighbour?: On mycorrhizal networks, Indra's Net, and the importance of building intentional connections between independent websites.
  • Yes, Buy Them a Coffee: Support and Mutual Aid on the IndieWeb: Asking for support isn't commodification, it's mutual aid.
  • The Internet Needs More Cross-Pollinators: We need people who move between different online subcultures to seed ideas and build bridges.
  • The IndieWeb is Wonderfully Dionysian: A plea to write your own comments, from the heart, instead of letting genAI do it for you.

Building It Yourself

  • Building an IndieAuth Comment System for Your Static Site: How to build a comment system for your static site using IndieAuth and Netlify Functions.
  • How Webmentions Work on brennan.day: A tutorial and walkthrough of implementing webmentions, from setup to display.
  • Why Make Your Website Accessible, Anyways?: Web accessibility isn't compliance theatre, it's about designing for everyone.
  • Phoneblogging: Why the IndieWeb must prioritize accessible, simple ways to blog from a phone.

The Bigger Picture

  • Building the Good Web: What do we owe each other, and what's the distance between knowing something is wrong and doing something about it?
  • Trust and Faith in Our Web: What is trust in an AI-saturated internet, and how do we make independent web spaces more accessible?
  • Good, Standard Work: Creating the Commons: From Garrett Hardin's tragedy of the commons to Elinor Ostrom's refutation, the commons was never inevitable to fail. It was always a choice.
  • How Are We Preparing for the Long Web?: Digital preservation, link rot, and building for the Internet decades from now.
  • Free Speech and the IndieWeb: Not all harm is equal, and where we draw the lines in the sand for what's acceptable.

(August 12, 2010) Perhaps the clearest and most citable marker of the term's formal retirement from mainstream professional use is when Google rebranded "Google Webmasters" to "Google Search Central" in 2020. An institutional funeral. "Merriam-Webster claims the first known use of the word 'webmaster' was in 1993, years before Google even existed. However, the term is becoming archaic, and according to the data found in books, its use is in sharp decline. A user experience study we ran revealed that very few web professionals identify themselves as webmasters anymore. They're more likely to call themselves Search Engine Optimizer (SEO), online marketer, blogger, web developer, or site owner, but very few 'webmasters.' In brainstorming our new name, we realized that there's not one term that perfectly summarizes the work people do on websites." — Google Search Central Blog (Nov 12, 2020) Part Two: NOW It is your innate human right to create. All of the above was pretext for this: You can be a webmaster right now. You can create a website right now. Yes, you. Your website can look however you want it to, and function in any way you want. It can have whatever you want on it. You can look up tutorials, and you can have your questions answered by humans just by joining forums, IRC channels, and independent platforms. The act of creating and learning inherently places you in the community. prelude: The Deception Generally speaking, we have been deceived into thinking many broad falsehoods: Regarding the webmaster: The Internet has become too complex for a single person to master all aspects of it. You must use a certain tool or platform to properly be part of this movement. Regarding the Internet: Technology is inherently addictive, and brings us harm. In order to stay connected to others online, we must use corporate social media platforms, become the product, and surrender our privacy. The Internet is primarily falsehoods, misinformation, and meaningless spam content. Regarding us: Most of us are incapable of learning technical, scientific, mathematical concepts. Those of us who are knowledgeable are reluctant to share information, and hostile to beginners. When plainly laid out like this, it's easy to see how we've been conned into a cynical, pessimistic—even misanthropic view of things. Companies worth billions of dollars have a bottom line that depends on the general population to continue believing all of the above. Our perspective on technology and other people has been greatly distorted into the negative. In reality, the Internet has terabytes of high-quality resources to learn from. There are thousands of people just like you looking for connection, hungry for a better vision of the future, wanting to cultivate nourishing hobbies. You are so capable. The idea that one person cannot master all aspects of the web, as the webmaster was once known to, is demonstrably false. Be optimistic about your capabilities and the willingness of others to help you. Be skeptical of anybody who attempts to divide or gatekeep, proclaiming the mandated use or superiority of a specific tool or platform. Likewise, I want to note that searching for "return of the webmaster" in 2026 may lead you to discussions of the "agentic web" or "orchestration," a euphemism for somebody who employs generative AI to do the multidisciplinary work that comes with being a webmaster. Those who manage a stack of expensive large language models, those who are prompt engineers for static site generators, and those who neglect to take the time to learn for themselves, unwilling to put in the effort themselves (or thinking they're incapable to). That's not what this is. My manifesto is not about becoming an orchestrator. Being a webmaster means becoming a sovereign creator. We are not reclaiming the title of "webmaster" only to then offload the work and art onto chatbots. We are reclaiming it because it is the only title that remains which still carries the weight of total, unapologetic human agency over our digital lives. a. The Bare Minimum is All You Need To be a Webmaster, you need a computer, a text editor, and a way to host. That's it. You don't need a degree in computer science. You don't need a $50/month subscription to a proprietary builder. You don't even need the money to buy a domain name if you don't have the cash. Use https://freedns.afraid.org/ to get a free domain. Throw your files up on Neocities or Nekoweb or web 1.0 hosting. Write your HTML in Notepad. Edit your CSS in TextEdit. If you don't have a computer or Internet yourself, you could be sitting in a public library on a recycled Chromium machine and still you have everything you need to become a Webmaster. There are not gatekeepers at the doors of the World Wide Web. Like many other things in life, the only lock is the one we put on our own ambitions. A Webmaster is not just a developer. You are a UX/UI designer, you are a writer and editor, you are an accessibility specialist, and an advocate for others to reclaim their digital autonomy. You are a creator, rather than a consumer. And you are capable of all these things. You will wrestle with semantic markup to make a page accessible. You will agonize over typeface kerning and colour palettes. You will write prose and publish your weird obsessions and link to your Internet neighbours. You will manage server logs, tweak the .htaccess file, and you will decide and design the architecture of your digital home. This is not a career path, this is a craft. This is the last best multidisciplinary sandbox, both creative and technical, all rendered on an index.html. And there is no wrong answer. Serve your website over the Gemini protocol. SSH into the Tildeverse and build a terminal-based homepage alongside strangers. Set up a homelab in your closet using the old, defunct family computer. There are a million ways to do this. The only wrong answer is sitting on the sidelines believing you don't belong in the arena with us. b. The Last Public Square Corporate social media platforms we used to call the "new public square" have been astroturf'd, bulldozed, and sold to the highest-bidding fascist oligarch. Your existence is a rental, your voice is a throttled lottery. Your so-called "community" is at the mercy of a billionaire's whim. Building your own website is an act of digital repatriation. Creating your own corner of the Internet reclaims one of the only mediums where we retain freedom, creativity, and autonomy. With the plethora of hosting options available, you can migrate if terms of service change to your disliking. There's no pay-to-play visibility. There's just you, text, and the open protocols of the web. c. The Myth of Incompetence The most effective way the power structures of our age have oppressed us is by making us feel as though we are stupid, as though we are incapable of learning. Many of us have been convinced coding is arcane magic, that servers are eldritch horrors, and that computer science is reserved for child prodigies and those who are privileged to just "naturally get it." A user who is afraid of the machine and doubts their own capabilities is one that will surrender and pay for a solution. You are not incapable. There is a lot to learn, yes. And the technologies are deep. But do not forget we are still living in the golden age of human knowledge—endless free resources, tutorials, wikis, and forums are available at your fingertips. I will repeat myself and say the only barrier that exists is the one you construct in your mind. You require grit, determination, and a "why." This is your why. The desire to express yourself. The hunger to build something truly of your own. The need to connect with other humans. d. Universalism Let me be clear: this is not about "IndieWeb" specs, it isn't about the "Small Web" or "SmolWeb." It isn't a retro-revival nostalgia trip, pining for GeoCities and AOL dial-up tones. Those are all labels, clubs, and memberships. Standards with elitism and in-group and cliques and gatekeeping as a result. What I'm talking about is universal. It's not about specific mechanics, it's about a philosophy. It is a big tent. It doesn't matter if you speak English. It doesn't matter if you don't know how to spell words right in your native tongue. It doesn't matter if you don't know a single line of JavaScript, either. And it certainly doesn't matter if you think you have "nothing interesting to say." I promise you do. All humans have value, we have our hobbies, our frustrations, our obsessions and small thoughts. Putting this in writing on a page you build with your own hands means you're contributing to a richer, stranger, more wonderful ecosystem. e. Those Who Came Before I stand on the shoulders of giants. I am not the first to write a web manifesto, nor the last. I myself am nobody special, nor anybody with authority. I am mere conduit for a message that desperately needs to be heard. I give credit to Tantek Çelik, Amber Case, Aaron Parecki, Crystal Beasley, and Kevin Marks for founding IndieWebCamp in Portland, Oregon in 2011. I give credit to Daniel Murray's melonking.net as a foundational "web revival" artifact. "[The web revival] is a riff on the 20th century American folk music revival, and it implies that early personal sites, like those hosted on GeoCities, were culturally significant as digital folk art." — Daniel Murray (Melonking), quoted in New_ Public (September 7, 2025) I give credit to webmistress Sadness, who has been sharing resources on web mastery for years, and was the founder of the now defunct Yesterweb, served as many people's first experience of the indie-web-crafting scene. "In the earlier iterations of this manifesto, I made the mistake of focusing too heavily on the creation of personal websites as the main method of fighting against the exploitative capitalist hellscape that has become our Internet... For example, we can work on transforming social relations online." — Sadness, Internet manifesto (May 2023) I give credit to James G., who has been blogging about the independent Internet for over six years, who hosts the podcast Wonders of Webweaving, and who has recently founded the Web Writers' Collective, which is open to anyone. I give credit to Alexandra and Kaylee for the community and resources of 32-bit Café. I give credit to Adam Newbold for the community and services of omg.lol. There are hundreds of people who have dedicated thousands of hours in trying to make the web more human and joyous for all. f. Saving the World We can create a more human web right now. The world is in dire straits, and I'm reminded of the words of Carl Sagan, coincidentally written at the dawn of the webmaster: “In our obscurity, in all this vastness, there is no hint that help will come from elsewhere to save us from ourselves.” — Carl Sagan, Pale Blue Dot (1994) There are those who see the act of webmastery as "only" a hobby and pastime—and I say this is not mutually exclusive to world-saving. The personal is political. Our ability to maintain our joy and ourselves is, itself, resistance. Here is another falsehood I want to emphasize: Our right to freely express ourselves is never a guarantee. The past thirty years of the Internet have been an explosive, chaotic experiment in the commons and the human condition. But the freedom of expression we've been granted is not a given or perpetual promise, and it is extremely foolish to think we will have this for the next ten years, let alone forever. Start as you are, with what you have, while you still have time to do so. Exercise your innate human right to create. Be a developer. Be a designer. Be a writer. Be a systems administrator. Be a philosopher. Be a Webmaster. It is the most punk rock, anti-establishment, liberating thing you can do in the 21st century. And yeah, it is fucking awesome. Now, go build something. Starting Out What I Have Learned Being on the IndieWeb for a Month: Small technical joys that turned solitude into dialogue, and treating the Internet like a personal playground and lab. Resources for the Personal Web: A Follow-Up Guide: Blogging platforms, search engines that prioritize small sites, and directories for finding like-minded creators. Softcore First, Hardcore Eventually: A Ladder for the IndieWeb: Why you should climb the rungs progressively instead of choosing between easy platforms and full technical independence on day one. Building It Yourself Building an IndieAuth Comment System for Your Static Site: How to build a comment system for your static site using IndieAuth and Netlify Functions. The Bigger Picture Building the Good Web: What do we owe each other, and what's the distance between knowing something is wrong and doing something about it? Trust and Faith in Our Web: What is trust in an AI-saturated internet, and how do we make independent web spaces more accessible? Free Speech and the IndieWeb: Not all harm is equal, and where we draw the lines in the sand for what's acceptable. You can think of the postmaster as an email administrator. The idea being that you can email postmater[sic] @ some domain, and always be connected directly to somebody that could fix a problem with the email. That remains a reserved name today on any email inbox. The webmaster served a pretty similar purpose on the web."
— Jay Hoffman, "What Happened to the Webmaster" (June 16, 2020)

blocks.html_en: iii. THE DECLINE (2008-2020)

sentences.en: iii.
sentences.zh: 三.

sentences.en: THE DECLINE (2008-2020)

blocks.html_en: As sites grew and the Internet evolved from the expectation of a handful of HTML files located in /var/www/html/ into instead a complex beast of software and content management systems, the "one person does everything" model stopped being the default, and the title became a culture-war topic among web professionals.

sentences.en: As sites grew and the Internet evolved from the expectation of a handful of HTML files located in /var/www/html/ into instead a complex beast of software and content management systems, the "one person does everything" model stopped being the default, and the title became a culture-war topic among web professionals.
sentences.zh: 随着网站的发展，互联网从 /var/www/html/ 中的少量 HTML 文件演变为复杂的软件和内容管理系统，“一个人做所有事情”模型不再是默认的，标题成为网络专业人士之间的文化战争话题。

blocks.html_en: Schisms grew from the complexity. The Internet became a vector for business, and then the way to make money as the dotcom bubble inflated. People needed to specialize, whether that was to design for the front-end, or program and administrate the server from the back-end. You needed usability specialists and network engineers and search engine optimizers.

sentences.en: Schisms grew from the complexity.
sentences.zh: 分裂源于复杂性。

sentences.en: The Internet became a vector for business, and then the way to make money as the dotcom bubble inflated.
sentences.zh: 互联网成为商业的载体，并随着互联网泡沫的膨胀而成为赚钱的方式。

sentences.en: People needed to specialize, whether that was to design for the front-end, or program and administrate the server from the back-end.
sentences.zh: 人们需要专业化，无论是为前端设计，还是从后端编程和管理服务器。

sentences.en: You needed usability specialists and network engineers and search engine optimizers.
sentences.zh: 您需要可用性专家、网络工程师和搜索引擎优化师。

Dammit Jim, I’m a Webmaster, not a Digital Government Web Content Communications and Application Development Knowledge Management Specialist! ...or am I?
Is the term webmaster an accurate description of the responsibilities of today’s web professional, or is that moniker just a quaint artifact from the simpler, earliest days of the web where someone akin to a similarly quaint notion of a Ringmaster juggled a circus of unwieldy text, spinning logos and blinking text?
— David Kitzmiller, FCC Webmaster, Mastering the Web: An Old-Fashioned Notion? (August 12, 2010)

blocks.html_en:
"Merriam-Webster claims the first known use of the word 'webmaster' was in 1993, years before Google even existed. However, the term is becoming archaic, and according to the data found in books, its use is in sharp decline. A user experience study we ran revealed that very few web professionals identify themselves as webmasters anymore. They're more likely to call themselves Search Engine Optimizer (SEO), online marketer, blogger, web developer, or site owner, but very few 'webmasters.' In brainstorming our new name, we realized that there's not one term that perfectly summarizes the work people do on websites."
— Google Search Central Blog (Nov 12, 2020)

sentences.en: You can create a website right now.
sentences.zh: 您现在就可以创建一个网站。

sentences.en: Yes, you.
sentences.zh: 是的，你。

sentences.en: Your website can look however you want it to, and function in any way you want.
sentences.zh: 您的网站可以按照您想要的方式显示，并按照您想要的方式运行。

sentences.en: It can have whatever you want on it.
sentences.zh: 它可以有你想要的任何东西。

blocks.html_en: You can look up tutorials, and you can have your questions answered by humans just by joining forums, IRC channels, and independent platforms. The act of creating and learning inherently places you in the community.

sentences.en: You can look up tutorials, and you can have your questions answered by humans just by joining forums, IRC channels, and independent platforms.
sentences.zh: 你可以查找教程，只需加入论坛、IRC 频道和独立平台即可让人工解答你的问题。

sentences.en: The act of creating and learning inherently places you in the community.
sentences.zh: 创造和学习的行为本质上使您融入社区。

blocks.html_en: prelude: The Deception

sentences.en: prelude: The Deception
sentences.zh: 前奏：欺骗

blocks.html_en: Generally speaking, we have been deceived into thinking many broad falsehoods:

sentences.en: Generally speaking, we have been deceived into thinking many broad falsehoods:
sentences.zh: 一般来说，我们被欺骗而产生了许多广泛的谎言：

blocks.html_en: Regarding the webmaster:

sentences.en: Regarding the webmaster:
sentences.zh: 关于站长：

blocks.html_en: • The Internet has become too complex for a single person to master all aspects of it.

sentences.en: The Internet has become too complex for a single person to master all aspects of it.
sentences.zh: 互联网已经变得过于复杂，一个人无法掌握它的所有方面。

blocks.html_en: • You must use a certain tool or platform to properly be part of this movement.

sentences.en: You must use a certain tool or platform to properly be part of this movement.
sentences.zh: 你必须使用某种工具或平台才能正确地参与这一运动。

blocks.html_en: Regarding the Internet:

sentences.en: Regarding the Internet:
sentences.zh: 关于互联网：

blocks.html_en: • Technology is inherently addictive, and brings us harm.

sentences.en: Technology is inherently addictive, and brings us harm.
sentences.zh: 技术本质上会让人上瘾，并给我们带来伤害。

blocks.html_en: • In order to stay connected to others online, we must use corporate social media platforms, become the product, and surrender our privacy.

sentences.en: In order to stay connected to others online, we must use corporate social media platforms, become the product, and surrender our privacy.
sentences.zh: 为了与他人在线保持联系，我们必须使用企业社交媒体平台，成为产品，并放弃我们的隐私。

blocks.html_en: • The Internet is primarily falsehoods, misinformation, and meaningless spam content.

sentences.en: The Internet is primarily falsehoods, misinformation, and meaningless spam content.
sentences.zh: 互联网主要是谎言、错误信息和毫无意义的垃圾邮件内容。

blocks.html_en: Regarding us:

sentences.en: Regarding us:
sentences.zh: 关于我们：

blocks.html_en: • Most of us are incapable of learning technical, scientific, mathematical concepts.

sentences.en: Most of us are incapable of learning technical, scientific, mathematical concepts.
sentences.zh: 我们大多数人都无法学习技术、科学、数学概念。

blocks.html_en: • Those of us who are knowledgeable are reluctant to share information, and hostile to beginners.

sentences.en: Those of us who are knowledgeable are reluctant to share information, and hostile to beginners.
sentences.zh: 我们这些有知识的人不愿意分享信息，并且对初学者充满敌意。

blocks.html_en: When plainly laid out like this, it's easy to see how we've been conned into a cynical, pessimistic—even misanthropic view of things. Companies worth billions of dollars have a bottom line that depends on the general population to continue believing all of the above.

sentences.en: When plainly laid out like this, it's easy to see how we've been conned into a cynical, pessimistic—even misanthropic view of things.
sentences.zh: 当这样简单地阐述时，很容易看出我们是如何被欺骗而对事物抱有愤世嫉俗、悲观甚至厌世的态度。

sentences.en: Companies worth billions of dollars have a bottom line that depends on the general population to continue believing all of the above.
sentences.zh: 价值数十亿美元的公司的底线取决于普通民众是否继续相信上述所有内容。

blocks.html_en: Our perspective on technology and other people has been greatly distorted into the negative. In reality, the Internet has terabytes of high-quality resources to learn from. There are thousands of people just like you looking for connection, hungry for a better vision of the future, wanting to cultivate nourishing hobbies. You are so capable.

sentences.en: Our perspective on technology and other people has been greatly distorted into the negative.
sentences.zh: 我们对技术和其他人的看法已经被极大地扭曲为消极的。

sentences.en: In reality, the Internet has terabytes of high-quality resources to learn from.
sentences.zh: 事实上，互联网拥有海量的优质资源可供学习。

sentences.en: There are thousands of people just like you looking for connection, hungry for a better vision of the future, wanting to cultivate nourishing hobbies.
sentences.zh: 有成千上万的人像您一样在寻找联系，渴望对未来有更美好的憧憬，想要培养有益的爱好。

sentences.en: You are so capable.
sentences.zh: 你真有能力。

blocks.html_en: The idea that one person cannot master all aspects of the web, as the webmaster was once known to, is demonstrably false.

sentences.en: The idea that one person cannot master all aspects of the web, as the webmaster was once known to, is demonstrably false.
sentences.zh: 正如网站管理员曾经所知道的那样，一个人无法掌握网络的所有方面的想法显然是错误的。

blocks.html_en: Be optimistic about your capabilities and the willingness of others to help you. Be skeptical of anybody who attempts to divide or gatekeep, proclaiming the mandated use or superiority of a specific tool or platform.

sentences.en: Be optimistic about your capabilities and the willingness of others to help you.
sentences.zh: 对自己的能力和他人帮助你的意愿保持乐观。

sentences.en: Be skeptical of anybody who attempts to divide or gatekeep, proclaiming the mandated use or superiority of a specific tool or platform.
sentences.zh: 对任何试图分裂或把关、宣扬特定工具或平台的强制使用或优越性的人持怀疑态度。

blocks.html_en: Likewise, I want to note that searching for "return of the webmaster" in 2026 may lead you to discussions of the "agentic web" or "orchestration," a euphemism for somebody who employs generative AI to do the multidisciplinary work that comes with being a webmaster. Those who manage a stack of expensive large language models, those who are prompt engineers for static site generators, and those who neglect to take the time to learn for themselves, unwilling to put in the effort themselves (or thinking they're incapable to).

sentences.en: Likewise, I want to note that searching for "return of the webmaster" in 2026 may lead you to discussions of the "agentic web" or "orchestration," a euphemism for somebody who employs generative AI to do the multidisciplinary work that comes with being a webmaster.
sentences.zh: 同样，我想指出，搜索“2026 年网站管理员回归”可能会引导您讨论“代理网络”或“编排”，这是对使用生成式人工智能来完成作为网站管理员所需的多学科工作的人的委婉说法。

sentences.en: Those who manage a stack of expensive large language models, those who are prompt engineers for static site generators, and those who neglect to take the time to learn for themselves, unwilling to put in the effort themselves (or thinking they're incapable to).
sentences.zh: 那些管理一堆昂贵的大型语言模型的人，那些成为静态站点生成器的及时工程师的人，以及那些忽视花时间自学、不愿意自己付出努力（或认为自己没有能力）的人。

blocks.html_en: That's not what this is. My manifesto is not about becoming an orchestrator. Being a webmaster means becoming a sovereign creator. We are not reclaiming the title of "webmaster" only to then offload the work and art onto chatbots. We are reclaiming it because it is the only title that remains which still carries the weight of total, unapologetic human agency over our digital lives.

sentences.en: That's not what this is.
sentences.zh: 事实并非如此。

sentences.en: My manifesto is not about becoming an orchestrator.
sentences.zh: 我的宣言并不是要成为一名协调者。

sentences.en: Being a webmaster means becoming a sovereign creator.
sentences.zh: 成为一名网站管理员意味着成为一名主权创造者。

sentences.en: We are not reclaiming the title of "webmaster" only to then offload the work and art onto chatbots.
sentences.zh: 我们收回“网站管理员”的头衔并不是为了将工作和艺术转移到聊天机器人上。

sentences.en: We are reclaiming it because it is the only title that remains which still carries the weight of total, unapologetic human agency over our digital lives.
sentences.zh: 我们正在收回它，因为它是唯一一个仍然在我们的数字生活中仍然承载着完全的、毫无歉意的人类代理权重的头衔。

blocks.html_en: a. The Bare Minimum is All You Need

sentences.en: a.
sentences.zh: 一个。

sentences.en: The Bare Minimum is All You Need
sentences.zh: 最低限度就是您所需要的

blocks.html_en: To be a Webmaster, you need a computer, a text editor, and a way to host. That's it.

sentences.en: To be a Webmaster, you need a computer, a text editor, and a way to host.
sentences.zh: 要成为一名网站管理员，您需要一台计算机、一个文本编辑器和一种托管方式。

sentences.en: That's it.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

blocks.html_en: You don't need a degree in computer science. You don't need a $50/month subscription to a proprietary builder. You don't even need the money to buy a domain name if you don't have the cash.

sentences.en: You don't need a degree in computer science.
sentences.zh: 您不需要计算机科学学位。

sentences.en: You don't need a $50/month subscription to a proprietary builder.
sentences.zh: 您不需要每月支付 50 美元订阅专有构建器。

sentences.en: You don't even need the money to buy a domain name if you don't have the cash.
sentences.zh: 如果你没有现金，你甚至不需要钱去购买域名。

blocks.html_en: • Use https://freedns.afraid.org/ to get a free domain.

sentences.en: Use https://freedns.afraid.org/ to get a free domain.
sentences.zh: 使用 https://freedns.afraid.org/ 获取免费域名。

blocks.html_en: • Throw your files up on Neocities or Nekoweb or web 1.0 hosting.

sentences.en: Throw your files up on Neocities or Nekoweb or web 1.0 hosting.
sentences.zh: 将您的文件放在 Neocities 或 Nekoweb 或 web 1.0 托管上。

blocks.html_en: • Write your HTML in Notepad. Edit your CSS in TextEdit.

sentences.en: Write your HTML in Notepad.
sentences.zh: 在记事本中编写 HTML。

sentences.en: Edit your CSS in TextEdit.
sentences.zh: 在 TextEdit 中编辑 CSS。

blocks.html_en: If you don't have a computer or Internet yourself, you could be sitting in a public library on a recycled Chromium machine and still you have everything you need to become a Webmaster. There are not gatekeepers at the doors of the World Wide Web. Like many other things in life, the only lock is the one we put on our own ambitions.

sentences.en: If you don't have a computer or Internet yourself, you could be sitting in a public library on a recycled Chromium machine and still you have everything you need to become a Webmaster.
sentences.zh: 如果您自己没有计算机或互联网，您可能坐在公共图书馆的一台回收的 Chromium 机器上，但仍然拥有成为网站管理员所需的一切。

sentences.en: There are not gatekeepers at the doors of the World Wide Web.
sentences.zh: 万维网的门口没有看门人。

sentences.en: Like many other things in life, the only lock is the one we put on our own ambitions.
sentences.zh: 就像生活中的许多其他事情一样，唯一的锁就是我们为自己的野心设置的锁。

blocks.html_en: A Webmaster is not just a developer. You are a UX/UI designer, you are a writer and editor, you are an accessibility specialist, and an advocate for others to reclaim their digital autonomy. You are a creator, rather than a consumer. And you are capable of all these things.

sentences.en: A Webmaster is not just a developer.
sentences.zh: 网站管理员不仅仅是开发人员。

sentences.en: You are a UX/UI designer, you are a writer and editor, you are an accessibility specialist, and an advocate for others to reclaim their digital autonomy.
sentences.zh: 您是 UX/UI 设计师、作家和编辑、无障碍专家，以及其他人收回数字自主权的倡导者。

sentences.en: You are a creator, rather than a consumer.
sentences.zh: 你是一个创造者，而不是一个消费者。

sentences.en: And you are capable of all these things.
sentences.zh: 而你有能力做所有这些事情。

blocks.html_en: You will wrestle with semantic markup to make a page accessible. You will agonize over typeface kerning and colour palettes. You will write prose and publish your weird obsessions and link to your Internet neighbours. You will manage server logs, tweak the .htaccess file, and you will decide and design the architecture of your digital home.

sentences.en: You will wrestle with semantic markup to make a page accessible.
sentences.zh: 您将努力使用语义标记来使页面易于访问。

sentences.en: You will agonize over typeface kerning and colour palettes.
sentences.zh: 您会为字体字距调整和调色板而苦恼。

sentences.en: You will write prose and publish your weird obsessions and link to your Internet neighbours.
sentences.zh: 你将写散文，发表你奇怪的痴迷，并链接到你的互联网邻居。

sentences.en: You will manage server logs, tweak the .htaccess file, and you will decide and design the architecture of your digital home.
sentences.zh: 您将管理服务器日志、调整 .htaccess 文件，并决定和设计数字家庭的架构。

blocks.html_en: This is not a career path, this is a craft. This is the last best multidisciplinary sandbox, both creative and technical, all rendered on an index.html.

sentences.en: This is not a career path, this is a craft.
sentences.zh: 这不是一条职业道路，这是一门手艺。

sentences.en: This is the last best multidisciplinary sandbox, both creative and technical, all rendered on an index.html.
sentences.zh: 这是最后一个最好的多学科沙箱，无论是创意还是技术，都在index.html 上呈现。

blocks.html_en: And there is no wrong answer. Serve your website over the Gemini protocol. SSH into the Tildeverse and build a terminal-based homepage alongside strangers. Set up a homelab in your closet using the old, defunct family computer. There are a million ways to do this. The only wrong answer is sitting on the sidelines believing you don't belong in the arena with us.

sentences.en: And there is no wrong answer.
sentences.zh: 并且没有错误的答案。

sentences.en: Serve your website over the Gemini protocol.
sentences.zh: 通过 Gemini 协议为您的网站提供服务。

sentences.en: SSH into the Tildeverse and build a terminal-based homepage alongside strangers.
sentences.zh: 通过 SSH 进入 Tildeverse 并与陌生人一起构建基于终端的主页。

sentences.en: Set up a homelab in your closet using the old, defunct family computer.
sentences.zh: 使用废弃的旧家庭电脑在您的衣柜中设置一个家庭实验室。

sentences.en: There are a million ways to do this.
sentences.zh: 有一百万种方法可以做到这一点。

sentences.en: The only wrong answer is sitting on the sidelines believing you don't belong in the arena with us.
sentences.zh: 唯一错误的答案是袖手旁观，认为你不属于我们的竞技场。

blocks.html_en: b. The Last Public Square

sentences.en: b.
The Last Public Square
sentences.zh: 最后的公共广场

blocks.html_en: Corporate social media platforms we used to call the "new public square" have been astroturf'd, bulldozed, and sold to the highest-bidding fascist oligarch. Your existence is a rental, your voice is a throttled lottery. Your so-called "community" is at the mercy of a billionaire's whim.

sentences.en: Corporate social media platforms we used to call the "new public square" have been astroturf'd, bulldozed, and sold to the highest-bidding fascist oligarch.
sentences.zh: 我们过去称之为“新公共广场”的企业社交媒体平台已被拆除、推平，并​​卖给出价最高的法西斯寡头。

sentences.en: Your existence is a rental, your voice is a throttled lottery.
sentences.zh: 你的存在是一种出租，你的声音是一张被限制的彩票。

sentences.en: Your so-called "community" is at the mercy of a billionaire's whim.
sentences.zh: 你们所谓的“社区”受亿万富翁一时兴起的摆布。

blocks.html_en: Building your own website is an act of digital repatriation.

sentences.en: Building your own website is an act of digital repatriation.
sentences.zh: 建立自己的网站是一种数字遣返的行为。

blocks.html_en: Creating your own corner of the Internet reclaims one of the only mediums where we retain freedom, creativity, and autonomy.

sentences.en: Creating your own corner of the Internet reclaims one of the only mediums where we retain freedom, creativity, and autonomy.
sentences.zh: 创建您自己的互联网角落，重新夺回了我们保留自由、创造力和自主权的唯一媒介之一。

blocks.html_en: With the plethora of hosting options available, you can migrate if terms of service change to your disliking. There's no pay-to-play visibility. There's just you, text, and the open protocols of the web.

sentences.en: With the plethora of hosting options available, you can migrate if terms of service change to your disliking.
sentences.zh: 借助大量可用的托管选项，如果服务条款发生您不喜欢的变化，您可以迁移。

sentences.en: There's no pay-to-play visibility.
sentences.zh: 没有付费播放的可见性。

sentences.en: There's just you, text, and the open protocols of the web.
sentences.zh: 只有您、文本和网络的开放协议。

blocks.html_en: c. The Myth of Incompetence

sentences.en: c.
The Myth of Incompetence
sentences.zh: 无能的神话

blocks.html_en: The most effective way the power structures of our age have oppressed us is by making us feel as though we are stupid, as though we are incapable of learning.

sentences.en: The most effective way the power structures of our age have oppressed us is by making us feel as though we are stupid, as though we are incapable of learning.
sentences.zh: 我们这个时代的权力结构压迫我们最有效的方式就是让我们感觉自己很愚蠢，好像我们没有学习能力。

blocks.html_en: Many of us have been convinced coding is arcane magic, that servers are eldritch horrors, and that computer science is reserved for child prodigies and those who are privileged to just "naturally get it."

sentences.en: Many of us have been convinced coding is arcane magic, that servers are eldritch horrors, and that computer science is reserved for child prodigies and those who are privileged to just "naturally get it."
sentences.zh: 我们中的许多人都相信编码是神秘的魔法，服务器是可怕的东西，计算机科学是神童和那些有幸“自然而然地掌握它”的人的专利。

blocks.html_en: A user who is afraid of the machine and doubts their own capabilities is one that will surrender and pay for a solution.

sentences.en: A user who is afraid of the machine and doubts their own capabilities is one that will surrender and pay for a solution.
sentences.zh: 害怕机器并怀疑自己能力的用户会投降并为解决方案付费。

blocks.html_en: You are not incapable. There is a lot to learn, yes. And the technologies are deep. But do not forget we are still living in the golden age of human knowledge—endless free resources, tutorials, wikis, and forums are available at your fingertips.

sentences.en: You are not incapable.
sentences.zh: 你并非无能。

sentences.en: There is a lot to learn, yes.
sentences.zh: 有很多东西需要学习，是的。

sentences.en: And the technologies are deep.
sentences.zh: 而且技术很深。

sentences.en: But do not forget we are still living in the golden age of human knowledge—endless free resources, tutorials, wikis, and forums are available at your fingertips.
sentences.zh: 但不要忘记，我们仍然生活在人类知识的黄金时代——无尽的免费资源、教程、维基和论坛触手可及。

blocks.html_en: I will repeat myself and say the only barrier that exists is the one you construct in your mind.

sentences.en: I will repeat myself and say the only barrier that exists is the one you construct in your mind.
sentences.zh: 我会重复一遍，并说唯一存在的障碍是你在脑海中构建的障碍。

blocks.html_en: You require grit, determination, and a "why." This is your why. The desire to express yourself. The hunger to build something truly of your own. The need to connect with other humans.

sentences.en: You require grit, determination, and a "why."
sentences.zh: 你需要勇气、决心和“为什么”。

sentences.en: This is your why.
sentences.zh: 这就是你的原因。

sentences.en: The desire to express yourself.
sentences.zh: 表达自己的愿望。

sentences.en: The hunger to build something truly of your own.
sentences.zh: 渴望构建真正属于自己的东西。

sentences.en: The need to connect with other humans.
sentences.zh: 与其他人联系的需要。

blocks.html_en: d. Universalism

sentences.en: d.
Universalism
sentences.zh: 普遍主义

blocks.html_en: Let me be clear: this is not about "IndieWeb" specs, it isn't about the "Small Web" or "SmolWeb." It isn't a retro-revival nostalgia trip, pining for GeoCities and AOL dial-up tones.

sentences.en: Let me be clear: this is not about "IndieWeb" specs, it isn't about the "Small Web" or "SmolWeb."
sentences.zh: 让我明确一点：这与“IndieWeb”规范无关，与“Small Web”或“SmolWeb”无关。

sentences.en: It isn't a retro-revival nostalgia trip, pining for GeoCities and AOL dial-up tones.
sentences.zh: 这不是一次复古复兴的怀旧之旅，不是对 GeoCities 和 AOL 拨号音的怀念。

blocks.html_en: Those are all labels, clubs, and memberships. Standards with elitism and in-group and cliques and gatekeeping as a result.

sentences.en: Those are all labels, clubs, and memberships.
sentences.zh: 这些都是标签、俱乐部和会员资格。

sentences.en: Standards with elitism and in-group and cliques and gatekeeping as a result.
sentences.zh: 结果是精英主义、内部集团、派系和把关的标准。

blocks.html_en: What I'm talking about is universal. It's not about specific mechanics, it's about a philosophy. It is a big tent.

sentences.en: What I'm talking about is universal.
sentences.zh: 我所说的是普遍性的。

sentences.en: It's not about specific mechanics, it's about a philosophy.
sentences.zh: 这与具体的机制无关，而是与哲学有关。

sentences.en: It is a big tent.
sentences.zh: 这是一个大帐篷。

blocks.html_en: It doesn't matter if you speak English. It doesn't matter if you don't know how to spell words right in your native tongue. It doesn't matter if you don't know a single line of JavaScript, either.

sentences.en: It doesn't matter if you speak English.
sentences.zh: 如果你会说英语并不重要。

sentences.en: It doesn't matter if you don't know how to spell words right in your native tongue.
sentences.zh: 如果您不知道如何用母语正确拼写单词也没关系。

sentences.en: It doesn't matter if you don't know a single line of JavaScript, either.
sentences.zh: 即使您不懂一行 JavaScript 也没关系。

blocks.html_en: And it certainly doesn't matter if you think you have "nothing interesting to say." I promise you do. All humans have value, we have our hobbies, our frustrations, our obsessions and small thoughts. Putting this in writing on a page you build with your own hands means you're contributing to a richer, stranger, more wonderful ecosystem.

sentences.en: And it certainly doesn't matter if you think you have "nothing interesting to say."
sentences.zh: 如果你认为自己“没什么有趣的可说”，那当然也没关系。

sentences.en: I promise you do.

content_html_zh:
一周前，当我为 2026 年 HTML Day 做项目时，我偶然发现了一篇关于眨眼和字幕标签的文章中的这段话：

当时，出现了新一代网络专业人士，他们自豪地被称为“网站管理员”。 网站管理员既是设计师，又是开发人员，又是传播者，他们拥有足够深奥的网络知识来管理、编辑和创建大大小小的网站。 — 杰伊·霍夫曼（Jay Hoffman，2017 年 8 月 28 日）

就在那时，一切都对我产生了影响。

在过去的一年里，我在独立网站上撰写了数十篇文章。 四十二篇关于原则、技术教程、可访问性和倡导的文章。

而且，在某种程度上，这一切都导致了这份宣言。 经过几个月的研究，认识了许多善良而有才华的人，并自己构建了一些东西，我才终于了解了站长的真正力量。

我认为这将是我写过的最重要的事情，我想与你们分享。 与大家一起。

第一部分：过去

最早的站长都是未经授权、自学成才、一人运营的。 第一位网站管理员是一位女性，斯坦福大学图书馆员路易丝·阿迪斯 (Louise Addis)。

我。 起源 (1993)

距离 Tim Berners-Lee 于 1990 年底命名 CERN 的第一个 Web 服务器，并于 1991 年 8 月 6 日发布第一个网站 info.cern.ch[1] 已经过去了几年。

网站管理员最初被理解为互联网上相当于现实世界的邮政局长。

“其他协议对于众所周知的邮箱名称有事实上的标准，例如 NNTP 的 USENET@domain（请参阅 [RFC977]）和 HTTP 的 WEBMASTER@domain（请参阅 [HTTP]）。” — RFC 2142，“公共服务、角色和功能的邮箱名称”，Dave Crocker，Internet Mail Consortium。 （1997 年 5 月）

该 RFC 与 <POSTMASTER@domain>（RFC 822 要求）一起巩固了“网站管理员”作为网站规范的协议级联系点角色的地位。

“‘网站管理员’这个词来自于最初的电子邮件规范中定义的类似角色，称为邮政局长，而邮政局长又来自类似名称的政府职位邮政局长。 您可以将邮政局长视为电子邮件管理员。 这个想法是，您可以向 postmater[sic] @ 某个域发送电子邮件，并且始终直接连接到可以解决电子邮件问题的人员。 如今，该名称仍然是任何电子邮件收件箱中的保留名称。 网站管理员在网络上的目的非常相似。”——Jay Hoffman，“网站管理员发生了什么”（2020 年 6 月 16 日）

因此，webmaster@domain 已经是与 HTTP 协议本身绑定的事实上的电子邮件收件箱地址。

不过，标签和标题很快就发展得远远不止于此。

“最初，它指的是那个沮丧的技术人员，他在未经公司授权的情况下建立了流氓 Web 服务器，在文本编辑器中手动编写 HTML，将文件通过 FTP 传输到服务器，并在业余时间回复所有传入的公司电子邮件，通常也未经公司授权。” — Brian Wold，“网站管理员怎么了？ （以及其他误导性标题）”（2006 年 5 月 12 日）

二. 黄金时代（1994-2001）

最让人联想到“网站管理员”的时代始于 90 年代中期，当时比佛利山庄互联网（现称为 GeoCities）推出。

“在社交网络或 Web 2.0 之前，关于网络的要点不是你在 GeoCities 上有个人资料，而是你有机会在它之外构建你的网络家园，你可以在集中式服务之外存在和发展。” — Olia Lialina，理查德·麦克马纳斯 (Richard MacManus) 在《网络文化》中引用（2025 年 3 月 7 日）

当人们意识到任何人都可以创建自己的网站时，一种文化就发展起来了。 88x31 按钮、眨眼睛、.GIF、网络环、访客计数器、留言簿。 一切都源于此时。

“1996 年，网络上充斥着黑黄条纹的动画 .gif，这些动画都陶醉于道路建设的隐喻...... “此网站正在建设中”是默认的主页免责声明，直到每个人都意识到网络的固有本质是它将永远处于建设中。” — Fresher Styles for Web Designers，O'Reilly（2008 年 12 月）

虽然 GeoCities 现在被人们所怀念，但它确实也有其问题和问题。 同样，当时还有其他平台，例如 Tripod、Angelfire 和 Homestead。 将历史修改为理想化的单一文化是很容易的。

“对于早期的网络制作者来说，这并不是天堂。 它甚至不是一个好的网络托管服务。 它是免费的，而且并不比其他网站更糟糕，这就是为什么网站管理员要忍受笨拙的页面构建器的痛苦、商业脚本被注入到页面中的干预、意外的文件删除等等……”——“GeoCities' Afterlife and Web History”，作者：Olia Lialin，One Terabyte of Kilobyte Age（2019 年 7 月 30 日）

2009 年雅虎关闭该平台时，超过 3800 万个页面被删除。

三. 衰落（2008-2020）

随着网站的发展，互联网从 /var/www/html/ 中的少量 HTML 文件演变为复杂的软件和内容管理系统，“一个人做所有事情”模型不再是默认的，标题成为网络专业人士之间的文化战争话题。

分裂源于复杂性。 互联网成为商业的载体，并随着互联网泡沫的膨胀而成为赚钱的方式。 人们需要专业化，无论是为前端设计，还是从后端编程和管理服务器。 您需要可用性专家、网络工程师和搜索引擎优化师。

该死的吉姆，我是一名网站管理员，而不是数字政府网络内容通信和应用程序开发知识管理专家！ ……还是我？ “网站管理员”这个词是对当今网络专业人士职责的准确描述，还是这个绰号只是网络早期较简单的时代的一个古怪的产物，当时类似于“表演大师”的类似古怪概念的人在笨拙的文本、旋转的徽标和闪烁的文本中杂耍？ — David Kitzmiller，FCC 网站管理员，《掌握网络：一个老式的概念？ （2010 年 8 月 12 日）

也许谷歌在 2020 年将“Google 网站管理员”更名为“Google 搜索中心”是该术语正式从主流专业用途中退出的最清晰、最容易引用的标志。 机构葬礼。

“韦氏词典声称‘网站管理员’一词的首次使用是在 1993 年，比谷歌还早几年。 然而，这个术语正在变得过时，根据书籍中的数据，它的使用正在急剧下降。 我们进行的一项用户体验研究表明，很少有网络专业人士认为自己是网站管理员。 他们更有可能称自己为搜索引擎优化者 (SEO)、在线营销人员、博客作者、网络开发人员或网站所有者，但很少称自己为“网站管理员”。 在集思广益地讨论我们的新名称时，我们意识到没有一个术语可以完美地概括人们在网站上所做的工作。”——Google 搜索中心博客（2020 年 11 月 12 日）

第二部分：现在

创造是你与生俱来的人权。

以上所有这些都是借口：你现在就可以成为一名网站管理员。 您现在就可以创建一个网站。 是的，你。 您的网站可以按照您想要的方式显示，并按照您想要的方式运行。 它可以有你想要的任何东西。

你可以查找教程，只需加入论坛、IRC 频道和独立平台即可让人工解答你的问题。 创造和学习的行为本质上使您融入社区。

前奏：欺骗

一般来说，我们被欺骗而产生了许多广泛的谎言：

关于站长：

  1. 互联网已经变得过于复杂，一个人无法掌握它的所有方面。
  2. 你必须使用某种工具或平台才能正确地参与这一运动。

关于互联网：

  1. 技术本质上会让人上瘾，并给我们带来伤害。
  2. 为了与他人在线保持联系，我们必须使用企业社交媒体平台，成为产品，并放弃我们的隐私。
  3. 互联网主要是谎言、错误信息和毫无意义的垃圾邮件内容。

关于我们：

  1. 我们大多数人都无法学习技术、科学、数学概念。
  2. 我们这些有知识的人不愿意分享信息，并且对初学者充满敌意。

当这样简单地阐述时，很容易看出我们是如何被欺骗而对事物抱有愤世嫉俗、悲观甚至厌世的态度。 价值数十亿美元的公司的底线取决于普通民众是否继续相信上述所有内容。

我们对技术和其他人的看法已经被极大地扭曲为消极的。 事实上，互联网拥有海量的优质资源可供学习。 有成千上万的人像您一样在寻找联系，渴望对未来有更美好的憧憬，想要培养有益的爱好。 你真有能力。

正如网站管理员曾经所知道的那样，一个人无法掌握网络的所有方面的想法显然是错误的。

对自己的能力和他人帮助你的意愿保持乐观。 对任何试图分裂或把关、宣扬特定工具或平台的强制使用或优越性的人持怀疑态度。

同样，我想指出，搜索“2026 年网站管理员回归”可能会引导您讨论“代理网络”或“编排”，这是对使用生成式人工智能来完成作为网站管理员所需的多学科工作的人的委婉说法。 那些管理一堆昂贵的大型语言模型的人，那些成为静态站点生成器的及时工程师的人，以及那些忽视花时间自学、不愿意自己付出努力（或认为自己没有能力）的人。

事实并非如此。 我的宣言并不是要成为一名协调者。 成为一名网站管理员意味着成为一名主权创造者。 我们收回“网站管理员”的头衔并不是为了将工作和艺术转移到聊天机器人上。 我们正在收回它，因为它是唯一一个仍然在我们的数字生活中仍然承载着完全的、毫无歉意的人类代理权重的头衔。

一个。 最低限度就是您所需要的

要成为一名网站管理员，您需要一台计算机、一个文本编辑器和一种托管方式。 就是这样。

您不需要计算机科学学位。 您不需要每月支付 50 美元订阅专有构建器。 如果你没有现金，你甚至不需要钱去购买域名。

  1. 使用 https://freedns.afraid.org/ 获取免费域名。
  2. 将您的文件放在 Neocities 或 Nekoweb 或 web 1.0 托管上。
  3. 在记事本中编写 HTML。 在 TextEdit 中编辑 CSS。

如果您自己没有计算机或互联网，您可能坐在公共图书馆的一台回收的 Chromium 机器上，但仍然拥有成为网站管理员所需的一切。 万维网的门口没有看门人。 就像生活中的许多其他事情一样，唯一的锁就是我们为自己的野心设置的锁。

网站管理员不仅仅是开发人员。 您是 UX/UI 设计师、作家和编辑、无障碍专家，以及其他人收回数字自主权的倡导者。 你是一个创造者，而不是一个消费者。 而你有能力做所有这些事情。

您将努力使用语义标记来使页面易于访问。 您会为字体字距调整和调色板而苦恼。 你将写散文，发表你奇怪的痴迷，并链接到你的互联网邻居。 您将管理服务器日志、调整 .htaccess 文件，并决定和设计数字家庭的架构。

这不是一条职业道路，这是一门手艺。 这是最后一个最好的多学科沙箱，无论是创意还是技术，都在index.html 上呈现。

并且没有错误的答案。 通过 Gemini 协议为您的网站提供服务。 通过 SSH 进入 Tildeverse 并与陌生人一起构建基于终端的主页。 使用废弃的旧家庭电脑在您的衣柜中设置一个家庭实验室。 有一百万种方法可以做到这一点。 唯一错误的答案是袖手旁观，认为你不属于我们的竞技场。

b. 最后的公共广场

我们过去称之为“新公共广场”的企业社交媒体平台已被拆除、推平，并​​卖给出价最高的法西斯寡头。 你的存在是一种出租，你的声音是一张被限制的彩票。 你们所谓的“社区”受亿万富翁一时兴起的摆布。

建立自己的网站是一种数字遣返的行为。

创建您自己的互联网角落，重新夺回了我们保留自由、创造力和自主权的唯一媒介之一。

借助大量可用的托管选项，如果服务条款发生您不喜欢的变化，您可以迁移。 没有付费播放的可见性。 只有您、文本和网络的开放协议。

c. 无能的神话

我们这个时代的权力结构压迫我们最有效的方式就是让我们感觉自己很愚蠢，好像我们没有学习能力。

我们中的许多人都相信编码是神秘的魔法，服务器是可怕的东西，计算机科学是神童和那些有幸“自然而然地掌握它”的人的专利。

害怕机器并怀疑自己能力的用户会投降并为解决方案付费。

你并非无能。 有很多东西需要学习，是的。 而且技术很深。 但不要忘记，我们仍然生活在人类知识的黄金时代——无尽的免费资源、教程、维基和论坛触手可及。

我会重复一遍，并说唯一存在的障碍是你在脑海中构建的障碍。

你需要勇气、决心和“为什么”。 这就是你的原因。 表达自己的愿望。 渴望构建真正属于自己的东西。 与其他人联系的需要。

d. 普遍主义

让我明确一点：这与“IndieWeb”规范无关，与“Small Web”或“SmolWeb”无关。 这不是一次复古复兴的怀旧之旅，不是对 GeoCities 和 AOL 拨号音的怀念。

这些都是标签、俱乐部和会员资格。 结果是精英主义、内部集团、派系和把关的标准。

我所说的是普遍性的。 这与具体的机制无关，而是与哲学有关。 这是一个大帐篷。

如果你会说英语并不重要。 如果您不知道如何用母语正确拼写单词也没关系。 即使您不懂一行 JavaScript 也没关系。

如果你认为自己“没什么有趣的可说”，那当然也没关系。 我保证你会的。 所有人类都有价值，我们有我们的爱好、我们的挫折、我们的痴迷和小想法。 将其写在您亲手构建的页面上意味着您正在为一个更丰富、更陌生、更美妙的生态系统做出贡献。

和。 那些来过的人

我站在巨人的肩膀上。 我不是第一个撰写网络宣言的人，也不是最后一个。 我自己并不是什么特别的人，也不是什么有权威的人。 我只是传达迫切需要被听到的信息的渠道。

我感谢 Tantek Çelik、Amber Case、Aaron Parecki、Crystal Beasley 和 Kevin Marks 于 2011 年在俄勒冈州波特兰创立了 IndieWebCamp。

“在这份宣言的早期版本中，我犯了一个错误，过于关注个人网站的创建，将其作为对抗已经成为我们互联网的剥削性资本主义地狱的主要方法...... 例如，我们可以致力于改变在线社会关系。”——悲伤，互联网宣言（2023 年 5 月）

f. 拯救世界

我们现在就可以创建一个更加人性化的网络。 世界正处于水深火热之中，我想起了卡尔·萨根在站长黎明时恰巧写下的一句话：

“在我们默默无闻的情况下，在这片广阔的土地上，没有任何迹象表明援助会来自其他地方来拯救我们。” ——卡尔·萨根，《淡蓝点》(1994)

有些人认为网站管理行为“只是”一种爱好和消遣——我说这与拯救世界并不相互排斥。 个人的就是政治的。 我们维持快乐和自我的能力本身就是抵抗。

我想强调的是另一个谎言：我们自由表达自己的权利永远无法得到保证。 过去三十年的互联网对公共空间和人类状况来说是一场爆炸性的、混乱的实验。 但我们所获得的言论自由并不是一个既定的或永久的承诺，认为我们将在未来十年内拥有这种自由是极其愚蠢的，更不用说永远了。

趁你还有时间，从你拥有的一切开始。

行使你与生俱来的创造人权。

成为一名开发人员。 成为一名设计师。 成为一名作家。 成为一名系统管理员。 成为一名哲学家。 成为一名网站管理员。

这是 21 世纪你能做的最朋克摇滚、反体制、最自由的事情。 是的，这太棒了。

我的其他独立网络文章

在过去的一年里，我写了四十二篇关于这个主题的文章。 以下是我认为最值得初学者花时间的内容。

开始

  • 我在 IndieWeb 上一个月学到的东西：将孤独转化为对话的小技术乐趣，并将互联网视为个人游乐场和实验室。
  • 个人网络资源：后续指南：博客平台、优先考虑小型网站的搜索引擎以及寻找志趣相投的创作者的目录。
  • 首先是软核，最终是硬核：独立网络的阶梯：为什么您应该逐步攀登阶梯，而不是在第一天就在简单平台和完全技术独立之间进行选择。
  • 1% 规则：致所有不在网上发布任何内容的人的公开信：呼吁 99% 只消费但从不创造的互联网用户采取行动。
  • 你不必写博客：你的网站可以是神殿、艺术或其他任何东西。 你不需要写一个字就属于这里。

社区和联系

  • 你不愿意做我的邻居吗？：关于菌根网络、因陀罗网，以及在独立网站之间建立有意连接的重要性。
  • 是的，请他们喝杯咖啡：IndieWeb 上的支持和互助：寻求支持不是商品化，而是互助。
  • 互联网需要更多的异花授粉者：我们需要在不同的在线亚文化之间流动的人来传播想法并建立桥梁。
  • IndieWeb 是奇妙的酒神式的：恳求您发自内心地写下自己的评论，而不是让 genAI 为您做这件事。

自己构建

  • 为静态站点构建 IndieAuth 评论系统：如何使用 IndieAuth 和 Netlify 函数为静态站点构建评论系统。
  • 网络提及如何在 brennan.day 上工作：实现网络提及（从设置到显示）的教程和演练。
  • 无论如何，为什么要让您的网站具有可访问性？：网络可访问性不是合规性的表演，而是为每个人进行设计。
  • 电话博客：为什么 IndieWeb 必须优先考虑通过电话访问、简单的博客方式。

更大的图景

  • 构建良好的网络：我们彼此欠对方什么？知道错误与采取行动之间的距离有多大？
